To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
epidermal growth factors regulate cytokine production by human thymic TE cells.
TE cells express EGF-R in vitro and in situ and that treatment of primary TE cell cultures with TGF-alpha or EGF increases TE cell-derived cytokine production.
epidermal growth factors and transforming growth factor-alpha regulate cytokine production in human thymus at a post-translational level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of cytokine production within the human thymic microenvironment.
the mechanisms by which thymic epithelium (TE) cells regulate the expression of cytokines.
the role of the thymus in the development of the immune response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EGF and TFG- alpha regulate the production of IL-1 and 6 in TE cells by increasing mRNA stability.
TGF-alpha and/or EGF may be involved in the regulation of IL-1 and/or IL-6 production by TE cells in vivo.
EGF and TFG-alpha are critical regulatory molecules that modulate the production of TE cell derived cytokines within the human thymic microenvironment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EGF and TFG-alpha are key regulators of cytokine expression in the human thyme.
TGF-alpha and IL-6 are important cytokines in the thymus, and that TGF-alpha is produced by thymic epithelium and acts on TE cells to increase IL-6 and IL-1 production.
TGF-alpha and TGF-beta are critical regulatory molecules in the thymus for production of TE-derived cytokines and may function as modulators of human thymocyte development in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EGF and TFG-alpha regulate the production of IL-1 and 6 by TE cells at the level of mRNA stability.
EGF and TGA regulate IL1 and IL-1 expression in human thymus epithelial cells.
EGF and TGA are critical regulators of TE cell-derived IL-1 and TGF-alpha, and that TE cells express both EGF-R and TGF-alpha.
